Government of the Northwest Territories, Department of Finance
The Northwest Territories income tax brackets and credit amounts are indexed every year with the federal index factor; the CRA collects the territorial tax with the federal tax.
Government of the Northwest Territories, Department of Finance

Remuneration subject to the payroll tax: salaries and wages, bonuses, gratuities, commissions and honoraria, vacation travel assistance, stock options, taxable allowances and benefits, employer RRSP contributions, retiring allowances. Registration within 21 days of the first pay. Reporting period by the estimated payroll of the year: monthly above 1,000,000, quarterly above 600,000, semi-annual above 200,000, annual otherwise, monthly during the season for a seasonal employer. Remittance return, even nil, by the 20th day of the month after the period; annual return by February 28.
Government of the Northwest Territories, Department of Justice
Sections 1 (remuneration), 3 (tax of 2% of the employee) and 5 (withholding by the employer)

Every employee pays a tax of 2% of the remuneration paid in the year, which the employer withholds from the remuneration. Remuneration: the employment income under s. 5(1), 6 and 7 of the Income Tax Act, except a pension paid after retirement and the amounts deductible under s. 8(1)(c) or 110(2) of that Act. An employee who normally works outside the territory owes the tax on the days worked in it.
Government of the Northwest Territories, Department of Justice
Section 2 (prescribed amount), sections 8 to 10 and Schedule A (reporting periods and returns)

Prescribed amount of 5,000: an employee who normally works outside the territory owes no tax when the remuneration from the employer in the year does not exceed it. Remittance by the 20th day of the month after the reporting period; annual return by February 28.
Table of the Year's Maximum Insurable Remuneration

Year's Maximum Insurable Remuneration of the Northwest Territories: 112,600 in 2025, 116,000 in 2026 (110,600 shared with Nunavut in 2024). Average provisional assessment rate of 2.40 per $100 of assessable payroll in 2026; the rate of each industry subclass is on WSCC Connect.

Annual Payroll Report, the actual payroll of the previous year and an estimate of the current year, due February 28. Directors of a corporation, business owners and the self-employed are not covered automatically; Personal Optional Coverage from 37% of the YMIR up to the YMIR.
WSCC Policy Manual, Policy 02.01 Employer Assessments

Assessment = (assessable payroll / 100) x the rate of the industry subclass, the payroll of each worker capped at the YMIR; minimum assessment of 200. Payment by March 31, or by instalments of March 31, May 31, July 31 and September 30 for an assessment of 1,000 or more.
